To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the PDZK1- or NHERF-1-mediated modulation of OAT4 activity may be important in the regulated organic anion handling of the kidney.
the functional activity and membrane localization of renal apical OAT4 is regulated by PDZK1/NHERF1 interaction.
OAT4 interacts with two PDZ-containing proteins, PDZK and NHERF, and that this interaction enhances OAT4 function.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the molecular mechanisms of renal organic anion handling.
the identification of novel proteins that interact with the PDZ domain containing proteins.

the modulation of the renal apical organic cation/anion exchangers (OCTs and OATs) and the renal basolateral anion exchangers, which are involved in the regulated renal handling of organic cations, organic anions, and their conjugates.

the PDZ interaction of OAT4 with PDZK and NHERF proteins modulates the transport activity of OAT.
the PDZ interaction modulates the functional activity of organic anion transporter OAT4.
PDZ proteins modulate the function of OAT4, which may be important for regulated apical organic acid transport.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the renal apical organic transporter OAT4 is regulated by PDZK1/NHERF1 interaction, which may play a role in the regulation of renal organic anion handling and in the maintenance of body homeostasis.
we have identified two PDZ proteins that interact with OAT4 and modulate its function.
OAT4, which is the major apical organic anions transporter in kidney, interacts with the PDZK1 protein and the NHERF1 protein.
The main takeaway from our work is that
OAT4, a member of the organic anion transporters, is a novel substrate of PDZK and NHERF.
PDZK1 can interact with the PDZ domain of OAT4.

OAT4, a member of the solute carrier organic anion transporter (SLC22A) family, interacts with PDZ domain-containing scaffolding proteins PDZK-1 and Na(+)/H(+) exchange regulatory factor 1 (NHERF1), which is a known regulator of the renal sodium-hydrogen exchanger NHE3.
